cues: Group A cells carry antigen A, and the plasma carries anti B. Group O cells carry no antigen, so O can be given to anyone: the universal donor.
Group A B plasma has no antibodies, so A B can receive from anyone: the universal recipient.
Separately, an Rh negative mother carrying an Rh positive baby can become sensitised, and her antibodies can attack a later Rh positive baby.
An anti D injection within seventy two hours of delivery prevents it.
text: Blood groups. Group A cells carry antigen A, and the plasma carries anti B. Group O cells carry no antigen, so O can be given to anyone: the universal donor. Group A B plasma has no antibodies, so A B can receive from anyone: the universal recipient. Separately, an Rh negative mother carrying an Rh positive baby can become sensitised, and her antibodies can attack a later Rh positive baby. An anti D injection within seventy two hours of delivery prevents it.
